name: Isorun

modes.label: MicroVM sandbox, per-second (public beta)
modes.note: Billed per second on allocated vCPU + GiB RAM from create() to destroy() or idle auto-destroy (timeoutSec, default 300 s idle, so every session carries up to a 5-min billed idle tail unless destroyed/hibernated explicitly). "No minimums". Hibernated = $0 (pricing page). 4 vCPU/8 GiB = $0.22/h (docs table). Homepage selector offers 1/2/4/8 vCPU; no hard vCPU/RAM cap published (max_vcpu 8 taken from the homepage selector). 4 GiB growable scratch disk included; egress/TLS/platform fees included in compute price. Basis verified 2026-09-28: "Every sandbox has an idle timeout (default 300 seconds, configurable per-create via timeoutSec)" (https://docs.isorun.ai/sandboxes/lifecycle); billed "every second from isorun.create() to sandbox.destroy() (or the auto-destroy timeoutSec timer)" (https://docs.isorun.ai/getting-started/pricing).

plans.name: Pay as you go (public beta)
plans.note: No plan fee. $50 one-time signup credit, no card. Concurrency limits exist ("concurrent sandboxes count against your limits") but are unpublished.

plans.name: Talk to us (custom)
plans.note: Homepage "Talk to us" CTA; no published enterprise tier or rates.

perf_source: computesdk: cold_start_tti median 16.83 ms (2026-08-07), burst_tti median 43.58 ms at 100 concurrent (2026-09-25), DAX total 32.79 s (2026-09-25, 8 vCPU / 15.7 GiB x86_64 env). No hpc CPU run.
caveats: Public beta pricing ($0.025/vCPU-h + $0.015/GiB-h, launched v1.0.0 2026-06-16); no change since.

Allocation billing assumed: the pricing page bills "by the second based on vCPU and RAM" with an allocation-based example (1 vCPU+1 GiB x 90 s = $0.001), although destroy() says cpuMs/memPeakBytes are "the numbers you are billed on".

Hibernation is $0 per the pricing page ("you pay nothing while the sandbox is paused"); storage price for explicit snapshot() checkpoints is unpublished (snapshot_gib_month 0 reflects hibernation only).
Persistent disks (Tigris-backed) cost $0.02/GB-month on data actually stored, plus normal compute while attached; forks add only divergent writes. Encoded as disk_gib_month.
Default idle auto-DESTROY after 300 s (not hibernate): state is lost unless you hibernate or raise timeoutSec; a raised timeout keeps billing idle time.
Concurrency/session limits, docker-in-VM and hypervisor (KVM microVM, VMM unnamed) unpublished. Org pinned to one region (US or EU); no regional price difference published.
No SSH: docs (llms-full.txt) list only WebSocket PTY terminal, WebSocket shell sessions, exec() and HTTPS port URLs as access methods (verified 2026-09-28).

Docs conflict on idle-timeout default: lifecycle page and SDK reference say 300 s; the Claude Managed Agents integration example says 'idle auto-destroy, default 600'. Timer can be disabled with 0 (then idle time bills indefinitely).
Port URLs: docs limits table says 'Auth: none; the sandbox ID is the credential' (homepage calls them 'signed'). Any TCP port can be exposed over HTTPS/WS; no raw TCP inbound.
Browser/computer-use image docker.io/isorun/computer-use:1 needs >= 2 vCPU and >= 4 GiB (docs sizing guidance) = $0.11/h minimum at list rates.

Allocation basis is corroborated by the API reference: a 1 vCPU / 1 GiB sandbox with uptime_ms 59000 but cpu_ms 48 and mem_peak 49 MB returns cost_cents 0.0007, which equals allocation price in dollars (0.04 $/h x 59 s = $0.00066), not a usage-based figure. The 'cost_cents' / costCents field appears to be denominated in dollars despite its name (pricing page: 90 s example = $0.001, costCents 'e.g. 0.00111').

fleet.verification: Public beta, no card; introductory credit.
fleet.notes: Documentation acknowledges concurrent sandboxes consume account quota but numeric limit and increase path not established. Homepage 30 sibling-forks demonstration is not an account entitlement.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: When the timer fires, the sandbox is destroyed.
snapshot_auto.note: Idle timeout (default 300 s, timeoutSec; 0 disables) DESTROYS the sandbox; state is only kept if you call hibernate() yourself (memory+processes+filesystem, $0 while hibernated). Conflict: the Claude Managed Agents integration page advertises 'Hibernate-on-idle' but then says the server-side TTL 'reaps' idle sandboxes; the lifecycle page and SDK reference say auto-destroy.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A checkpoint captures a sandbox's full state so you can restore it later or fork it into parallel copies.
snapshot_on_demand.note: sandbox.snapshot() / POST /v1/runs/{id}/snapshot on a running VM; isorun.restore(id) boots a new sandbox from it (same region); snapshots persist until deleteSnapshot(). fork(n) clones a running sandbox: 'Each child inherits filesystem + memory state at fork time'. Memory included (changelog: 'checkpoint a running VM'). Separate disk-level snapshotDisk/forkDisk for persistent disks (copy-on-write).

harness_api.quote: The Isorun SDK ships a self-hosted adapter that
harness_api.note: No Isorun API to start/stream/follow-up an agent harness; the REST API is sandbox lifecycle, exec (JSON + SSE), PTY/shell WebSockets, files, snapshots, audit, network. Closest: runOrchestrator() adapter makes Isorun the self-hosted sandbox backend for Anthropic Claude Managed Agents (one microVM per Anthropic session; prompts/events/follow-ups go through Anthropic's Managed Agents API, not Isorun's). Also OpenAI Agents/LangChain/CrewAI tool integrations and an MCP server that drive sandboxes, not a harness.

egress_allowlist.quote: Policy is enforced outside guest code execution.
egress_allowlist.note: Per-sandbox network: {allow, deny} at create: CIDRs, IP literals, hostnames matched against SNI, wildcards (*.openai.com). Deny evaluated first; default unrestricted. Named profiles: unrestricted, locked-down (deny-all), claude-code, openai. Enforced at host boundary ('Code running in the sandbox can't edit iptables, swap the resolver, or otherwise disable the policy'). Set at create time; no live-update endpoint listed.

egress_http_rules.quote: A request through the credential proxy is forwarded only if its
egress_http_rules.note: Endpoint rules (credentials_v2, REST only for now) restrict method + path prefix/glob per credential, e.g. only POST /v1/chat/completions; anything else rejected with 4xx. Applies only to traffic through the credential proxy (the 5 recognised services), not to arbitrary egress.

ingress_rules.note: Ports are reachable only via <apiUrl>/v1/runs/<id>/proxy/<port>/ requiring the account API key as Bearer (401 otherwise); no public IP, no raw TCP. Docs contradict themselves: the same page's 'Authentication model' section says 'The URL is anonymous: anyone with the URL can hit it' and the Limits table says 'Auth: none; the sandbox ID is the credential'; the SDK reference sides with 'authenticated'. No per-port exposure choice, IP allowlist or share tokens.

guest_firewall.note: 'It boots a microVM with its own kernel' (VMM unnamed); root inside OCI images presumably but not stated. Network-filtering page: 'Changes made inside the VM only affect the guest's view', consistent with guest-side rules working but not overriding host enforcement.

secret_proxy.quote: The agent never sees the real secret.
secret_proxy.note: Real host-side reverse proxy; guest sees placeholders (OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-isorun-proxy-managed + *_BASE_URL pointing at 169.254.169.254 proxy). BUT only a fixed set of known services: openai, anthropic, google (Gemini), github (api.github.com), huggingface ('The proxy maps each credential map key to a known service.'). GitHub API makes it slightly more than LLM-only; arbitrary hosts, git-over-SSH, databases not covered. Method/path endpoint rules on top.

volume_attach.note: Named persistent disks (Tigris Cloud Disk, real ext4 block device with NVMe write-back cache) mounted at /workspace; createDisk/listDisks/snapshotDisk/forkDisk/deleteDisk; $0.02/GB-month stored; global, attach from any region. Only at create time (one disk per sandbox). Note: published npm isorun@1.0.3 types have no disk option yet (docs ahead of SDK or REST-only).

volume_shared.quote: One sandbox holds a disk at a time.
volume_shared.note: Tigris lease: 'a concurrent attach fails until the first detaches'. Sharing is via copy-on-write forks (independent copies), not concurrent mounts. No read-only multi-attach.

nested_virt.quote: Isorun runs your code in real microVMs, hardware-isolated sandboxes that boot in milliseconds.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No docs mention /dev/kvm or a second virtualization layer inside the guest; microVM hosts (Firecracker-class) essentially never expose nested KVM to tenants, and nothing on the site suggests an exception.

anti_bot.quote: The image ships Xvfb (a virtual display), a window manager, Chromium started
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The browser/computer-use image is a plain Chromium in a virtual display for agent-driven browsing; no stealth/fingerprint-evasion feature is documented anywhere in the docs.

captcha_solving.quote: The image ships Xvfb (a virtual display), a window manager, Chromium started
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Isorun is a general microVM sandbox/compute runtime; no CAPTCHA-solving API or integration is mentioned anywhere in the docs, changelog, or homepage.

egress_ip_type.quote: The VM gets a new guest IP on resume, so any ESTABLISHED outbound TCP connection from before hibernation is reset.
egress_ip_type.note: Isorun runs sandboxes as regular cloud-hosted microVMs (US/EU regions) with no public IPv4 and no residential/mobile IP product; outbound traffic is plain datacenter cloud IP space, changing on resume.

wake_on_request.quote: Resume restores a hibernated sandbox. The same runID is reused
wake_on_request.note: A hibernated sandbox only comes back via an explicit sandbox.resume() SDK/API call; nothing in the port-forwarding or lifecycle docs describes an incoming HTTP/proxy request auto-waking a stopped or hibernated sandbox.

live_resize.note: The only update-in-place API on a running sandbox is PATCH /v1/runs/{id}, which resets the idle timer. There is no endpoint or SDK method to change vCPU/RAM of a running sandbox; resizing requires creating a new sandbox (optionally from a fork/snapshot).

own_agent_api.quote: The Isorun SDK ships a self-hosted adapter that
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Isorun is a sandbox/compute runtime; its integrations (Claude Managed Agents, OpenAI Agents, LangChain, CrewAI, MCP server) all drive third-party agent frameworks or your own code inside the sandbox. There is no first-party Isorun browser/computer-use/research agent with its own driving API.

lang_python.note: Python is available out of the box by selecting the python:3.12-slim (or any Python) OCI image at create() time; nearly every SDK/integration example (code_interpreter tools, CrewAI, LangChain) runs Python this way. No dedicated first-party Python SDK is shipped yet ('Isorun Python SDK (in development)').

lang_node.quote: Official Node.js client for sandbox lifecycle, command execution, file I/O, snapshots, fork, hibernate, and port exposure.
lang_node.note: Node.js is the first-party SDK language (the Isorun client itself is the Node/TypeScript SDK) and the default sandbox base image is node:22-slim per the SDK reference.

static_egress_ip.quote: The VM gets a new guest IP on resume, so any ESTABLISHED outbound TCP connection from before hibernation is reset.
static_egress_ip.note: The guest's outbound IP changes across hibernate/resume cycles, and no fixed/static egress IP product is documented or priced anywhere (network.ipv4_available is false in this card).

self_host.quote: Isorun runs your code in real microVMs, hardware-isolated sandboxes that boot in milliseconds.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Isorun is a hosted SaaS runner (US/EU regions, per-second billing via API key); there is no downloadable runtime/appliance to run the microVM host on your own infrastructure. 'Self-hosted' in the Claude Managed Agents integration refers to Isorun acting as the self-hosted sandbox *for Anthropic's* Managed Agents API, not to running Isorun itself on-prem.

byoc.quote: Isorun runs your code in real microVMs, hardware-isolated sandboxes that boot in milliseconds.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No docs, pricing, or homepage content mentions deploying the Isorun runner into a customer-owned AWS/GCP/Azure account; it is a single multi-tenant SaaS with a US or EU region choice.

open_source.note: Only the client SDK (github.com/isorun/sdk, MIT-licensed) is open source; the sandbox runtime/microVM host itself is closed-source hosted infrastructure with no public repo or self-host distribution.

hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope for now. The homepage lists only a pending SOC 2 Type II attestation as a compliance milestone for this public-beta product; no HIPAA/BAA mention anywhere in docs or site.

sso.quote: No plan fee. $50 one-time signup credit, no card.
sso.note: not offered: outside the product's scope for now. This is a self-serve public-beta API product (sign up, get an API key); no SAML/OIDC/SSO feature, enterprise auth page, or mention is documented anywhere.

max_session_h.quote: Use sandbox.setTimeout(seconds) to extend it during a long-running workflow, pass 0 to disable.
max_session_h.note: No documented hard cap on total sandbox lifetime; only an idle auto-destroy timer exists (default 300s), which can be disabled (timeoutSec 0) or reset via PATCH, and a running/actively-used sandbox otherwise persists (billed) until you call destroy().

ssh.note: Full docs dump (2752 lines) list only exec(), WebSocket PTY/shell sessions, and HTTPS port proxying as access methods. The only 'SSH' hit in the whole corpus is 'a long-running node server.js, a jupyter notebook kernel, an SSH agent, they all survive' hibernation - describing an in-guest process surviving, not an SSH access method offered by Isorun. No sshd, no SSH key management, no ssh:// endpoint anywhere in docs or homepage.

public_ipv4.quote: The sandbox ID is the only credential on a public URL.
public_ipv4.note: Only access to sandbox network services is via HTTPS/WebSocket proxy URLs of the form <apiUrl>/v1/runs/<runID>/proxy/<port>/...; no dedicated/public IPv4 address is issued or documented anywhere ('ipv4', 'static ip', 'public ip' do not appear in the docs corpus). Consistent with raw_tcp_inbound already false.

agent_harnesses.quote: The SDK ships a self-hosted adapter for Anthropic Claude Managed Agents. Each Anthropic session is bound to its own sandbox for the lifetime of the session.
agent_harnesses.note: runOrchestrator() and the OpenAI Agents/LangChain/CrewAI/MCP integrations are client-side adapters that drive Isorun sandboxes from other vendors' agent frameworks/harnesses; Isorun itself exposes no API to start/stream/manage an agent harness (its REST/SDK surface is sandbox lifecycle, exec, PTY/shell, files, snapshots, network - matches the card's existing harness_api:false evidence).

gpu.quote: sandbox is a real Linux box with its own kernel, built for AI agents
gpu.note: No mention of 'gpu' anywhere in the 2752-line full docs dump, the homepage, or the lifecycle/pricing pages; the product is described purely as CPU/RAM-billed microVMs (vCPU-h + GiB-h pricing, no GPU SKU or GPU image). DuckDuckGo search for 'isorun.ai GPU sandbox' returns nothing relevant. Product is a general-purpose CPU agent-sandbox, not a GPU offering.

windows.quote: Each isorun.create() boots a microVM with its own kernel and defaults to
windows.note: Every example boots Linux OCI images (e.g. 'isorun.create({ image: "ubuntu:24.04" })'); no Windows image, guest OS option, or mention of 'windows' anywhere in the docs corpus or homepage. Isorun is a Linux-only microVM sandbox product.

macos.quote: Each microVM gets its own kernel.
macos.note: No mention of macOS/Darwin guest support anywhere in docs or homepage; sandboxes run Linux OCI images on KVM microVMs. macOS guest virtualization is outside what this product is.

arm64.note: The card's own third-party benchmark source records the test environment as x86_64; no arm64/aarch64 architecture option is mentioned anywhere in Isorun's docs, homepage, or changelog. No evidence of an ARM64 image/architecture choice.

soc2.note: Homepage pricing feature list explicitly marks SOC 2 Type II as upcoming/not-yet-certified, confirming false for the current state.
